_meta.description: Verified general legal information for students in Germany, used by Student Rights Check. Every statement the tool makes must come from this file. Nothing here is advice for an individual case.
_meta.verified_by: Manual check against law texts and official/authoritative sources listed in each entry
_meta.region_note: Federal law applies everywhere. University (exam) rules are verified for Bavaria (RaPO / BayHIG / AGVwGO); housing values marked 'München' are Munich-specific.

exam_sick_withdrawal.title: Sick on exam day: withdraw immediately with a doctor's certificate
exam_sick_withdrawal.summary: At Bavarian universities of applied sciences, the reasons for withdrawing from or missing an exam must be reported to the university immediately (unverzüglich) in writing and made credible. For illness you need a medical certificate based on an examination that, as a rule, took place on the exam day itself. Courts apply a strict standard: reporting weeks later is too late. Many universities accept the certificate up to the third day after the exam, but check your own APO.

exam_appeal.title: Disagree with an exam decision: objection or lawsuit, your choice
exam_appeal.summary: In Bavaria, against a personal exam decision (e.g. a failed exam) you may choose to either file an objection (Widerspruch) with the university or go directly to the administrative court. The deadline is normally one month and is stated in the legal remedy notice (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung) of the decision. Against an exmatriculation after finally failing, only a lawsuit is possible (Art. 12 Abs. 2 AGVwGO).

exam_inspection.title: You can usually see your marked exam
exam_inspection.summary: An exam is an administrative procedure. Exam regulations normally give students the right to inspect their marked exam, the examiner's comments and oral exam protocols after the result is published. Where and how long you can do this is set in your university's exam regulations, so check your APO/SPO and ask the exam office. Inspecting your exam is usually the first step before an objection.

exam_disadvantage_comp.title: Chronic illness or disability: you can apply for Nachteilsausgleich
exam_disadvantage_comp.summary: Students with a disability or chronic (also psychological) illness can apply for adjustments in exams (Nachteilsausgleich), e.g. more time or a separate room. In Bavaria this follows from the Bavarian Higher Education Innovation Act (BayHIG) and the exam regulations. You apply in advance with a medical certificate. A short-term illness is not a reason for Nachteilsausgleich; then withdrawing from the exam is the right path.

exam_maternity.title: Pregnant students are protected by the Maternity Protection Act
exam_maternity.summary: Since 2018 the Maternity Protection Act also applies to students. During the protection period (normally 6 weeks before and 8 weeks after birth) you have the right not to take exams and are exempt from compulsory courses, excursions and lab work. You can choose to take part anyway with a written declaration, which you can withdraw at any time.

minimum_wage.title: Minimum wage applies to Werkstudenten and Minijobs too
minimum_wage.summary: The statutory minimum wage is 13.90 EUR gross per hour from 1 January 2026 and 14.60 EUR from 1 January 2027. It applies to working students and mini-jobbers as well.

internship_wage.title: Internships: when you must get minimum wage
internship_wage.summary: Interns are generally entitled to minimum wage. Exceptions: a compulsory internship required by your study regulations, an orientation internship of up to 3 months before studies, and a first voluntary internship of up to 3 months alongside your studies with the same company. A voluntary internship longer than 3 months must be paid minimum wage from day one.

werkstudent_20h.law: Werkstudentenprivileg (§ 6 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 SGB V, § 27 Abs. 4 SGB III)
werkstudent_20h.title: Werkstudent: max. 20 hours a week during the semester
werkstudent_20h.summary: As a Werkstudent you pay no health, care or unemployment insurance contributions from your job (only pension insurance) as long as you work no more than 20 hours a week during the lecture period. More hours are fine in the semester break, at evenings, nights or weekends, but in total not more than 26 weeks a year above 20 hours. The amount you earn does not matter.

minijob_limit.title: Minijob earnings limit: 603 EUR a month in 2026
minijob_limit.summary: A Minijob may pay on average at most 603 EUR a month in 2026 (7,236 EUR a year) and 633 EUR from 2027. The limit is linked to the minimum wage. Minijobbers have the same rights as other employees: paid holiday, sick pay, minimum wage.

sick_pay.title: Sick pay: up to 6 weeks, also for Werkstudenten and Minijobs
sick_pay.summary: If you cannot work because of illness, your employer must keep paying your wage for up to six weeks per illness. The right starts after the job has lasted four weeks without interruption. It applies to part-time, Werkstudent and Minijob employees just like full-time staff.

minimum_vacation.title: Minimum paid holiday: 4 weeks per year, also part-time
minimum_vacation.summary: Every employee, including Werkstudenten and Minijobbers, has at least 24 working days of paid holiday per year based on a 6-day week. For fewer working days it is calculated pro rata: days per week x 24 / 6 (e.g. 2 days a week = 8 days, 3 days = 12 days, 5 days = 20 days).

probation_max.title: Notice periods: 2 weeks in probation (max. 6 months), then 4 weeks
probation_max.summary: During an agreed probation period, the job can be ended with two weeks' notice, but for at most six months. After that the normal notice period applies: four weeks to the 15th or the end of a month.

written_termination.title: Termination of a job must be on paper and signed
written_termination.summary: Ending an employment relationship by notice or termination agreement requires written form (signed paper). Electronic form is excluded, so a termination by e-mail or WhatsApp is not valid.

payslip_reference.title: You have a right to a payslip and a job reference
payslip_reference.summary: With every wage payment you are entitled to a payslip in text form showing the period and how your pay is made up. When the job ends, you are entitled to a reference (Arbeitszeugnis); on request a qualified one that also rates your performance and conduct. This also applies to student jobs.

working_hours.title: Working time: max. 8 (10) hours a day, breaks, 11 hours rest
working_hours.summary: Working time may normally not exceed 8 hours per working day; up to 10 hours are allowed if the average over 6 months stays at 8. If you work more than 6 hours you need at least 30 minutes break (45 minutes above 9 hours); you may not work more than 6 hours in a row without a break. Breaks can be split into blocks of at least 15 minutes. Between two shifts you need at least 11 hours of rest.

short_term_job.title: Holiday job: up to 3 months or 70 working days without social contributions
short_term_job.summary: A short-term job (kurzfristige Beschäftigung), e.g. a semester-break job, is free of social insurance contributions if it is limited in advance to at most 3 months or 70 working days in a calendar year, regardless of pay. All short-term jobs in the year are added up. It is still taxable, but you can usually get the tax back with a tax return.

equal_pay_parttime.title: Same job, same hourly pay: Minijobbers can't be paid less
equal_pay_parttime.summary: Part-time employees, including Minijobbers and working students, may not be treated worse than comparable full-time staff without an objective reason. The Federal Labour Court decided in January 2023 that a Minijobber with the same qualification and the same tasks must get the same hourly wage as full-time colleagues.

interview_questions.title: Job interview: forbidden questions and the 'right to lie'
interview_questions.summary: Employers may only ask questions related to the job. Questions about pregnancy or family planning, religion, sexual orientation, party or union membership are generally not allowed. If you are asked such a question, you may refuse or even answer untruthfully (the courts' 'right to lie') without the employer being able to cancel your contract later for that reason. Questions about qualifications, languages or work permit are allowed and must be answered truthfully.

intl_work_days.title: Non-EU students: 140 full or 280 half working days per year
intl_work_days.summary: With a student residence permit (§ 16b AufenthG) you may work up to 140 full days or 280 half days per calendar year without approval of the employment agency. A half day is up to 4 hours. Student assistant jobs at the university (studentische Nebentätigkeit) are not counted. Voluntary internships count, compulsory internships do not. Working more than allowed can put your permit at risk, so ask the Ausländerbehörde or the international office if unsure.

deposit_max.title: Deposit is capped at 3 months' cold rent
deposit_max.summary: For a flat or WG room, the deposit (Kaution) may be at most three times the monthly rent without operating costs (Nettokaltmiete). An agreement that is worse for the tenant is invalid, and you can claim back the part above the limit.

deposit_installments.title: You may pay the deposit in 3 monthly parts
deposit_installments.summary: If the deposit is a sum of money, the tenant is entitled to pay it in three equal monthly instalments. The first is due when the tenancy starts, the others together with the next rent payments. The landlord must keep the deposit separate from his own money in a bank account. A clause demanding the full amount up front cannot take this right away.

deposit_return.title: Getting your deposit back after moving out
deposit_return.summary: There is no fixed legal deadline for returning the deposit. The landlord gets a reasonable time to check his claims, usually about 3 to 6 months, sometimes longer if a utility bill (Nebenkostenabrechnung) is still due, for which he may keep a reasonable part. His claims for damage to the flat expire six months after he gets the flat back (§ 548 BGB). After that time, ask in writing for a deposit statement and payment with a deadline. Your own claim expires after three years.

tenant_notice.title: Tenant notice period is 3 months
tenant_notice.summary: A tenant can give notice by the third working day of a month, effective at the end of the month after next (about 3 months). A longer notice period to the tenant's disadvantage is invalid. Exceptions exist, e.g. for furnished rooms inside the landlord's own flat (§ 549 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 BGB) and for agreed waivers of notice, so this one is worth getting checked.

rent_brake.title: Mietpreisbremse: new rent max. 10% above local comparative rent
rent_brake.summary: In areas with a tight housing market, the rent at the start of a new tenancy may be at most 10% above the local comparative rent (in Munich: the Mietspiegel). In Bavaria this applies in 285 cities and municipalities including Munich and is extended until 31 December 2029. Exceptions exist (new buildings first rented after 1 Oct 2014, comprehensive modernisation, higher previous rent), and the landlord must tell you about them before signing.

rent_increase_cap.title: Rent increase cap: max. 15% in 3 years in Munich
rent_increase_cap.summary: In an ongoing tenancy the landlord can ask you to agree to an increase up to the local comparative rent, but in Munich (and other listed Bavarian municipalities) the rent may not rise by more than 15% within three years (instead of 20% elsewhere). Increases due to modernisation follow other rules.

rent_reduction.title: Defects (mould, pests, no heating): the rent is reduced by law
rent_reduction.summary: If the flat has a defect that reduces its use, e.g. mould, a pest infestation (cockroaches, mice, bedbugs) or no heating, the rent is reduced by law for as long as the defect exists. You must report the defect to the landlord immediately; if you do not, you can lose the right to reduce. In residential leases this right cannot be excluded by contract (§ 536 Abs. 4 BGB). How much you may reduce depends on the case, and paying too little can risk a termination, so get advice before cutting the rent.

landlord_entry.title: Your landlord may not enter your room without your consent
landlord_entry.summary: Once you rent a flat or room, you hold the right to decide who enters. The landlord needs a concrete reason (e.g. repairs, meter reading, viewing for a sale), must announce the visit in advance (often at least 24 hours, for viewings longer) and needs your consent. Only in a real emergency (burst pipe, gas leak, fire) may he enter without asking. Contract clauses allowing entry at any time without notice are invalid.

sublet.title: Subletting part of your flat: you can ask for permission
sublet.summary: If after signing the lease you get a legitimate interest (e.g. saving money, a semester abroad), you can demand the landlord's permission to sublet part of your flat. You always need the permission first. Since a BGH ruling of January 2026, subletting to make a profit is not a legitimate interest. A clause that excludes this right is invalid (§ 553 Abs. 3 BGB).

registration.title: Register your address within 2 weeks; the landlord must confirm
registration.summary: When you move into a flat, you must register at the registration office (Bürgerbüro / KVR in Munich) within two weeks. The landlord or main tenant must give you a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung within two weeks; a rental contract does not replace it. Missing these duties can be fined up to 1,000 EUR, on both sides.

cosmetic_repairs.law: § 307, § 535 BGB; BGH VIII ZR 185/14, VIII ZR 361/03
cosmetic_repairs.title: Moved into an unrenovated flat: you usually don't have to paint when you leave
cosmetic_repairs.summary: If you got the flat or room unrenovated and without fair compensation, a standard clause making you do the cosmetic repairs (painting, wallpapering) is invalid (BGH, 18 March 2015). Clauses with rigid schedules (e.g. 'kitchen every 3 years') are also invalid, as are clauses making you pay a share of future repairs when you move out early. Then the landlord can only demand the flat back in the state you received it. You must be able to prove that it was unrenovated, so take photos at move-in.

utility_bill.title: Utility bill (Nebenkostenabrechnung): 12-month deadlines for both sides
utility_bill.summary: The landlord must send the utility bill at the latest 12 months after the end of the billing period. If it arrives later, he can usually no longer demand extra payments (unless he is not responsible for the delay). You in turn have 12 months after receiving the bill to raise objections; after that you generally cannot. You may ask to see the receipts before you pay.

fixed_term_lease.title: Fixed-term lease only with a written reason, otherwise it is open-ended
fixed_term_lease.summary: A residential lease can only be limited in time if the landlord tells you a legal reason in writing when signing (e.g. he wants to live there himself or will renovate/demolish). Without such a reason the lease counts as open-ended, and you can give the normal 3-month notice. Furnished rooms in the landlord's own flat and short-term rentals follow different rules.

landlord_termination.title: The landlord needs a legal reason to give you notice
landlord_termination.summary: In a normal (open-ended) lease the landlord can only give ordinary notice if he has a legitimate interest, e.g. personal need (Eigenbedarf) or serious breaches by the tenant. Notice to raise the rent is not allowed. His notice period is at least 3 months and grows to 6 months after 5 years and 9 months after 8 years. Exceptions apply to furnished rooms in the landlord's own flat.

tenant_selfdisclosure.title: Flat applications: some questions a landlord may not ask
tenant_selfdisclosure.summary: In a tenant self-disclosure (Mieterselbstauskunft) landlords may ask about income, profession, household size and pets. Questions about religion, ethnic origin or political views are not allowed. You also have the right to know which of your data the landlord stores, why and for how long.

bafoeg.title: BAföG: up to 992 EUR a month in 2026
bafoeg.summary: The maximum BAföG for students not living with their parents is 992 EUR a month (475 EUR basic need + 380 EUR housing + health/care insurance supplement). Half is a grant, half an interest-free loan. BAföG is not paid retroactively before the month you apply, so apply early. A reform with higher rates is planned; according to the government draft of August 2026 the first increase comes on 1 April 2027 (not yet law).

kindergeld.title: Kindergeld continues during studies until age 25
kindergeld.summary: Parents receive Kindergeld of 259 EUR a month (2026) for a child in education or university studies up to the 25th birthday. During a first degree, side jobs do not affect it. Kindergeld is only paid retroactively for 6 months from the application.

broadcast_fee.title: Rundfunkbeitrag: exemption with BAföG (not living with parents)
broadcast_fee.summary: The broadcasting fee (18.36 EUR a month per flat) applies to every household. Students who receive BAföG and do not live with their parents can apply to be exempt. Without BAföG, a hardship application (Härtefall) is possible if your income is very low. In a WG the fee is paid once per flat, so share it.

tax_refund.title: Student job: you can often get your wage tax back
tax_refund.summary: Up to 12,348 EUR taxable income in 2026 no income tax is due for a single person. If wage tax was deducted from your student job, you can usually get it back by filing a tax return (Einkommensteuererklärung) for that year, e.g. via ELSTER. You can file voluntarily for the past four years.

wohngeld.title: Wohngeld: only if you are not eligible for BAföG in principle
wohngeld.summary: Students who are eligible for BAföG in principle get no housing benefit (Wohngeld), even if they receive no BAföG because their parents earn too much. Wohngeld is possible if BAföG is excluded in principle (e.g. age limit exceeded, maximum funding period over, late change of subject) or if BAföG is paid only as a full loan. You first need a BAföG rejection 'dem Grunde nach' from the BAföG office.

basic_account.title: Every person living legally in the EU has a right to a basic bank account
basic_account.summary: Banks offering accounts to consumers must open a basic account (Basiskonto) for anyone legally resident in the EU, including people without a fixed address and asylum seekers. It works on a credit basis (no overdraft) and offers deposits, withdrawals, transfers, direct debits and a debit card. Useful for international students whose application was rejected.

health_insurance.title: Health insurance: family insurance until 25, student rate until 30
health_insurance.summary: Health insurance is compulsory to enrol. Until your 25th birthday you can be insured free of charge through your parents' public insurance, if you earn at most 565 EUR a month (603 EUR in a Minijob) in 2026. After that, the student health insurance (KVdS) at a reduced rate applies, at most until the end of the semester in which you turn 30. After that you continue as a voluntary member at higher rates.

withdrawal_online.title: Bought online or by phone: 14 days to withdraw
withdrawal_online.summary: For contracts made online, by phone or at your door you can withdraw within 14 days without giving reasons. For goods the period starts when you receive them. If the seller did not inform you properly about this right, it lasts up to 12 months and 14 days. Declare the withdrawal clearly, e.g. by e-mail; just sending the item back is not always enough.

auto_renewal.title: Contracts may not silently renew for another fixed term
auto_renewal.summary: For consumer contracts concluded since 1 March 2022 (gym, phone, streaming, magazines...), a standard clause that automatically renews the contract for another fixed period is invalid. Automatic renewal is only allowed for an indefinite period, and the customer must then be able to cancel at any time with max. one month's notice.

consumer_notice.title: Notice before the end of the minimum term: max. 1 month
consumer_notice.summary: For consumer contracts concluded since 1 March 2022, a standard clause requiring notice of more than one month before the end of the initial term is invalid.

phone_contract.title: Phone and internet contracts: max. 24 months, then cancel monthly
phone_contract.summary: The initial term of a mobile or internet contract may not exceed 24 months, and the provider must also offer a contract of max. 12 months. After the initial term, a contract that renews silently can be cancelled at any time with one month's notice, at no cost. Early 'extensions' may not push the total binding term beyond 24 months.

cancel_button.title: Online subscriptions: a 'cancel contract' button is mandatory
cancel_button.summary: Companies that let consumers sign up for ongoing contracts on a website must also offer an easy online cancellation button ('Verträge hier kündigen' → 'jetzt kündigen'). If they don't, you can cancel at any time without notice. When ordering online, the final button must clearly say that you pay ('zahlungspflichtig bestellen' or equally clear); otherwise no contract is formed.

unordered_goods.title: Received something you didn't order: you don't have to pay
unordered_goods.summary: If a company sends you goods or services you did not order, it gets no claim against you: you do not have to pay, send them back or keep them safe. Exceptions: if it was obviously sent to you by mistake and you could see that, or if you ordered and got an equivalent substitute with a note that you may refuse it at the seller's cost.

data_access.title: You can ask any company what data it has about you
data_access.summary: Under the GDPR you can ask any company, landlord, employer or university whether and which personal data it stores about you, and get a free copy. You do not need to give a reason. They must answer within one month; in complex cases they may extend by two months but must tell you within the first month.

discrimination_housing.title: Rejected for a flat because of your origin: that is illegal
discrimination_housing.summary: Landlords and estate agents may not treat you worse when renting because of your ethnic origin (also national origin). This applies even to small private landlords. In January 2026 the BGH confirmed that estate agents are liable too. You can claim damages and compensation, but you must do so within two months, in writing. Keep evidence (e.g. same application under another name).

abmahnung_cap.title: Copyright warning letter: lawyer fees are capped for private people
abmahnung_cap.summary: If a private person who did not use the work commercially receives a first warning letter (Abmahnung), the lawyer fees they can be asked to pay are calculated on a value of max. 1,000 EUR for the injunction claim. This does not cap damages. A warning letter that does not meet the transparency rules of § 97a Abs. 2 UrhG is invalid. Do not ignore the deadline and do not sign the attached declaration before it is checked.

exams: Your student council (Studierendenvertretung / AStA) – many offer free legal advice on exam law
Exam office and student advisory service of your university
work: Free legal advice at your Studierendenwerk or student council
DGB students' advice / your trade union
international: Ausländerbehörde (immigration office) – ask before you exceed your working days
housing: Mieterverein in your city (e.g. Mieterverein München; low yearly fee, legal advice included)
Free legal advice offered by many Studierendenwerke and student councils
money: BAföG office (Amt für Ausbildungsförderung) of your Studierendenwerk
health: Your health insurance company (Krankenkasse) – they have to advise you
consumer: Verbraucherzentrale in your federal state (Verbraucherzentrale Bayern)
data: Data protection authority (in Bavaria: BayLDA for companies)
copyright: A lawyer for copyright law – do not sign anything before it is checked
